Measurement refuted the big fear (engram export is manifest-tracked → NOT re-materialized, only the delta chunk) and confirmed the real residual (stale manifest → chunk-based pull degraded in the window). Residual ruling: transitional degradation ACCEPTED, conditioned on short+embargoed window, DECLARED never silent.

1. Explicit pull EMBARGO block (runbook + PR body): between cutover-PR merge and C4 merge, NO chunk-based memory:pull on any clone.
2. Window minimized by scheduling: C4 is the NEXT slice, closes at C4 merge, scheduled immediately.
3. Step 5 post-cutover criteria = MEASURED numbers 275/3/4/0 + index 136 unique.
4. Final runbook step = open cutover PR (Part of #222, branch cutover/records-v1) with the real migrate report pasted in body; the merge is the cutover closure + final CP-C2b-2 evidence.
5. Embargo made concrete: names PCStaFe30-174 (~/code/brain, feature/v2.0.0, synced 2026-07-08, 31 chunks) — that machine must not pull until C4 merges.
6. Measured dedup cause 275→136: 47 physical chunk files, pre-cutover manifest references only 23, so 24 orphans from manifest churn (superseded snapshots committed without reference) with overlapping observations; migrate-v1 reads FILES not the manifest → captures orphans (correct) → reindex collapses by content-hash → 136 unique. Explains the second consumer's "31 imported".

Verified (read-only, real store byte-untouched): chunk files=47, manifest references=23, orphans=24 — addition 6 CONFIRMED exact. Clarified the apparent 23 (pre-cutover) vs 24 (post-share = 23 + 1 delta) as NOT a contradiction. Raised one enforcement caveat: a written embargo relies on human discipline; if a clone's session-start hook auto-pulls chunk-based, the embargo can break silently → confirm hook or pause it on PCStaFe30-174 for the window.
